title: Acids, Bases and pH

cards.b: Lemon juice, vinegar, stomach juices, soap, toothpaste, rain: all are acids or bases. Acid-base chemistry controls digestion, soil fertility, cleaning, pool water, and the Taj Mahal's marble.

• Arrhenius (1884-87): acids give H+ in water; bases give OH-.
  • Brønsted-Lowry (1923): acids donate protons (H+); bases accept them.
  • Lewis (1923): acids accept electron pairs; bases donate them.

Example: HCl + H2O → H3O+ + Cl-. HCl donates a proton, so it is an acid; water accepts it, so it acts as a base.

A strong acid ionises almost fully: HCl, H2SO4, HNO3. A weak acid ionises only partly and sets up an equilibrium: acetic acid (vinegar), citric acid, carbonic acid. Strong bases: NaOH, KOH. Weak base: ammonia (NH3).

Strength is not concentration. A dilute strong acid and a concentrated weak acid can both be possible.

Søren Sørensen, 1909. pH = -log10 [H+]. Each unit is a tenfold change.

pH 3 has 10 times more H+ than pH 4. Human blood is held tightly at about 7.4. Stomach acid is around pH 1.5 to 3.5.

Acid + base → salt + water.

HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O.

Antacids such as magnesium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide (the fizz): 2HCl + CaCO3 → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2.

Indicators show the pH: litmus (red in acid, blue in base), phenolphthalein (pink in base), universal indicator (rainbow).

A buffer resists pH change. It contains a weak acid and its salt (conjugate base). Added acid is mopped up by the base; added base by the acid. Blood uses the carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer. Without it, a little acidic food could be fatal.

[H+] = 1 x 10^-3 mol/L. pH = 3.

0.01 M HCl (strong): [H+] = 0.01 = 10^-2, pH = 2.

Neutralisation: how many mL of 0.1 M NaOH neutralise 20 mL of 0.1 M HCl? 1:1 ratio, same concentration, so 20 mL. If NaOH were 0.2 M, you need 10 mL.

• pH 7 is neutral only at 25 °C.
  • pH is not linear. pH 2 is 10 times more acidic than pH 3 and 100 times more than pH 4.
  • Strong does not mean concentrated.
  • Neutralisation does not always give pH 7 (weak acid with strong base gives a basic salt solution).

Turmeric is a natural indicator: yellow in acid, turning reddish in base, which is why soap-washed turmeric stains turn red. Acid rain from sulphur dioxide of nearby industry was found to yellow the Taj Mahal's marble (calcium carbonate). The Supreme Court's 1996 orders (M.C. Mehta case) led to the Taj Trapezium Zone and shifts to cleaner fuel.

• Brønsted-Lowry: acids donate H+, bases accept.
  • pH = -log [H+]; each unit is 10x.
  • Acid + base → salt + water; buffers resist pH change.
